intro: Follow the opening rhythm through a horn call, a lyrical E♭-major theme, fragmented development and an extended C-minor coda. The score is aligned automatically; timings are provisional, especially in quiet passages and the oboe cadenza, and have not been checked by ear.
question: How much can Beethoven build from three short notes and one?

cues.title: A rest, then the motto
cues.text: After a quaver rest, three Gs fall to a held E♭. Three Fs then fall to D, tied across two bars. The fermatas interrupt the pulse; the second gesture already changes the first rather than copying it mechanically.
cues.evidence: Bars 1–5, occurrence 1: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violinoone.ly and violoncello.ly, write rest–G–G–G, E♭ with fermata, then rest–F–F–F and D tied through bar 5 with fermata. Timing aligned automatically; fermata releases remain unreviewed.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: The rhythm changes register
cues.text: The first violins repeat A♭ and hold F while the lower strings answer with three Gs leading to C. Follow the short-short-short-long rhythm between registers rather than expecting the opening pitches to remain fixed.
cues.evidence: Bars 25–33, occurrence 1: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violinoone.ly has A♭ quavers followed by tied F; violoncello.ly has G–G–G in bars 28 and 32, answered by C in bars 29 and 33. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: The horn call
cues.text: The horns turn the motto into a call: three B♭s, then E♭, F and a lower B♭. The repeated-note rhythm survives, but the widening intervals prepare the E♭-major second group.
cues.evidence: Bars 59–62, occurrence 1: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, cornies.ly. Horns in E♭ write G–G–G, C, D, G, sounding B♭–B♭–B♭, E♭, F, B♭. The call starts after the opening quaver rest of bar 59. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: A melody above the motto
cues.text: The first violins begin the second theme in E♭ major, marked dolce — sweetly. Their B♭–E♭–D–E♭ line moves in longer notes; below it, the cellos keep three short B♭s leading to E♭. Contrast arrives without abandoning the opening rhythm.
cues.evidence: Bars 63–70, occurrence 1: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violinoone.ly gives the piano, dolce crotchet melody; violoncello.ly has B♭ quavers in bars 65 and 69, resolving to E♭. Timing aligned automatically; REPORT.md flags weak onset detection in this quiet passage.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: Downward runs, upward bass
cues.text: In the closing group, the first violins descend through short slurred and detached figures while the bass moves through accented chord tones. Listen to the opposing directions: the upper line falls even as the lower line helps drive the cadence forward.
cues.evidence: Bars 99–103, occurrence 1: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violinoone.ly has D–C–A♭–F, then C–B♭–G–E♭; violoncello.ly moves from A♭ to B♭ before the cadential continuation. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: The long premiere concert
cues.text: The Fifth was first performed at Vienna’s Theater an der Wien on 22 December 1808. The programme also included the Sixth Symphony, Fourth Piano Concerto and Choral Fantasy. These works shared one concert, not a sequence of separate premieres.
cues.evidence: Beethoven-Haus Bonn’s Vienna chronology, 1808 entry: https://www.beethoven.de/en/g/zeittafel-beethoven-in-wien
cues.how: Documented fact.

cues.title: The exposition repeats
cues.text: The opening returns because the exposition repeat is taken. This is not yet the recapitulation: bars 1–124 again carry the music from C minor to E♭ major before the development begins.
cues.evidence: Bar 1, occurrence 2: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, the repeat volta encloses bars 1–124 in the orchestral parts. The rest and repeated Gs restart here. score.json records both traversals; timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: The transition on its return
cues.text: On this second traversal, listen to the repeated Cs in the lower strings while the first violins climb into a more active line. The rhythm links the transition to the motto even when sustained notes and moving quavers exchange places.
cues.evidence: Bars 33–41, occurrence 2: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violoncello.ly alternates C attacks and rests; violinoone.ly moves from E♭–G–C into repeated-note and rising quaver figures. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: E♭ major a second time
cues.text: The dolce violin theme returns in the same key as before, E♭ major. Keep its first leap, B♭ up to E♭, in mind: at the recapitulation the corresponding melody will begin G–C instead.
cues.evidence: Bars 63–66, occurrence 2, compared with bars 307–310, occurrence 1: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violinoone.ly writes B♭–E♭–D–E♭–F–C–C–B♭, later transposed to G–C–B–C–D–A–A–G. Timing aligned automatically; quiet-passage timing is provisional.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: Several works at once
cues.text: Beethoven began sketching the Fifth in 1804 and completed it in 1808. Work on Fidelio, the “Razumovsky” quartets and the Appassionata sonata intervened; the symphony was not composed in one uninterrupted burst.
cues.evidence: Eastman School of Music, Symphony No. 5, composition history: https://www.esm.rochester.edu/beethoven/symphony-no-5/
cues.how: Documented fact.

cues.title: The repeat nears its boundary
cues.text: The descending violin figures and E♭-major closing gestures recur. This time the repeat sign will not send the orchestra back: the next large section keeps the rhythmic cell but leaves the exposition’s route behind.
cues.evidence: Bars 99–124, occurrence 2: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violinoone.ly repeats the descending quavers, held E♭ and G, and closing chords before the volta ends. The performed order then continues to bar 125, occurrence 1. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: Development starts with the horns
cues.text: The horns launch another three-short-note gesture, but it leads to a held G. The strings answer with D♭–D♭–D♭ falling to C. Familiar rhythm now connects contrasting pitches rather than restarting the exposition.
cues.evidence: Bars 125–128, occurrence 1: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, cornies.ly has written G quavers and held E, sounding B♭ and G; violinoone.ly and violoncello.ly enter in bar 126 on repeated D♭ before C. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: Fragments trade places
cues.text: The development breaks the material into short replies: the first violins hold D, then climb through G–B♭–C. The cellos run downward while the horns repeat the motto’s rhythm. No single line carries a complete opening theme.
cues.evidence: Bars 165–170, occurrence 1: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violinoone.ly alternates D with G–B♭–C; violoncello.ly descends through B♭–A and G–F–E♭–D; cornies.ly has repeated short attacks. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: Reduced to isolated notes
cues.text: The exchanges shrink towards single held notes separated by rests. The first violins move B♭–C♭–D♭, then settle much lower on C♯. Listen for the gaps between orchestral replies as well as the notes themselves.
cues.evidence: Bars 210–221, occurrence 1: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violinoone.ly writes B♭, C♭, D♭ and low C♯ minims with intervening whole-bar rests; the parts mark diminuendo and progressively softer dynamics. Timing aligned automatically; this thinning passage is not an isolated onset claim.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: The opening becomes the recapitulation
cues.text: The G–G–G–E♭ motto returns, now reinforced by wind and brass parts absent from the opening attacks. This begins the recapitulation, not another exposition repeat; the later second group will stay centred on C.
cues.evidence: Bars 248–252, occurrence 1, compared with bars 1–5, occurrence 1: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violinoone.ly restores the motto; oboi.ly and cornies.ly join its repeated notes and fermatas instead of their opening rests. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: The oboe suspends the pulse
cues.text: Within this bar, the oboe holds G over a fermata, then plays an unaccompanied Adagio: F–E♭–D, a short turn and another descent. The strings stop after their opening chord. The normal orchestral pulse resumes only after this interruption.
cues.evidence: Bar 268, occurrence 1: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, oboi.ly has a held G, Adagio F–E♭–D, E♭–D–C–D and F–E♭–D; violinoone.ly has one chord then rests. The entire cadenza remains bar 268. Timing aligned automatically; its short notes and fermata releases need aural review.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: Bassoons, then C major
cues.text: The earlier horn call now belongs to the bassoons: G–G–G, C, D, G. The violin melody follows in C major, with G rising to C. Both the instrumental colour and the key change while the second group’s outline survives.
cues.evidence: Bars 303–310, occurrence 1: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, fagotti.ly gives the transposed call in bars 303–306; violinoone.ly begins G–C–B–C at bar 307. Compare bars 59–66, occurrence 1. Timing aligned automatically; the quiet violin passage remains provisional.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: A semitone presses towards G
cues.text: Near the end of the second group, violins and cellos circle G through F♯ and A. The repeated semitone F♯–G makes the dominant insistently audible before the closing material expands.
cues.evidence: Bars 339–344, occurrence 1: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violinoone.ly and violoncello.ly repeat F♯–G and A–G crotchet pairs, ending with further F♯–G alternation. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: Deafness before the Fifth
cues.text: Beethoven’s Heiligenstadt Testament dates from 1802 and describes his increasing deafness. The Fifth’s first sketches followed in 1804. The document and the symphony belong to different moments; the score supplies no literal programme based on the letter.
cues.evidence: Beethoven-Haus’s chronology records the document under 1802: https://www.beethoven.de/en/g/zeittafel-beethoven-in-wien ; Eastman dates the symphony’s first sketches to 1804: https://www.esm.rochester.edu/beethoven/symphony-no-5/
cues.how: Documented fact.

cues.title: The coda changes the ground
cues.text: The coda holds C high in the violins while the bass changes underneath: C, A♭, E and F. Repeated upper notes no longer mean settled harmony. This extended ending develops the material again rather than merely adding final chords.
cues.evidence: Bars 374–381, occurrence 1: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violinoone.ly alternates held and tremolo C; violoncello.ly moves through C, A♭, E♮ and F in two-bar spans. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: A descending sequence
cues.text: A short violin figure keeps stepping down: E♭–D–F–E♭ becomes D–C–E♭–D, then C–B♭–D–C. Listen for the repeated shape at changing heights, while the lower parts descend in their own slower steps.
cues.evidence: Bars 410–414, occurrence 1: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violinoone.ly writes these successive quaver groups; violoncello.ly descends through B♭–C, A♭–B♭, G–A♭, F–G and E♭–F. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: Wind replies to strings
cues.text: Short string figures alternate with repeated Gs in the winds. Hear the changes of orchestral group across the rests: the coda can keep moving without a continuous melody in any one part.
cues.evidence: Bars 446–451, occurrence 1: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violinoone.ly has B–C–D–B figures separated by rests; oboi.ly answers with repeated G octaves in bars 448–449. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: The opening holds return
cues.text: The opening’s held E♭ returns under a fermata. Three Fs then fall to the tied D once more. Even near the end, Beethoven interrupts the pulse with the same unequal holds that framed the movement’s first five bars.
cues.evidence: Bars 479–482, occurrence 1: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violinoone.ly and violoncello.ly have E♭ with fermata, rest–F–F–F, then D tied across two bars with fermata. Compare bars 2–5, occurrence 1. Timing aligned automatically; actual releases are not established.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: The final C-minor cadence
cues.text: The final replies alternate dominant tension with C-minor chords. Listen for B♮ rising to C and for E♭, the minor third, in the closing harmony. This movement ends in minor; a major-key ending has not been secured here.
cues.evidence: Bars 491–502, occurrence 1: Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violinoone.ly and oboi.ly alternate B/G or B/D/G with C/E♭/G sonorities; violoncello.ly alternates G and C before the final C. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

transitions.title: Silence clears space for the horn call
transitions.how: Bar 56 cuts off A–C–E♭–G♭, a diminished seventh over C; bar 57 is silent. A short B♭-major chord over D in bar 58 supplies E♭ major’s dominant, then releases the ensemble. This medial caesura separates the two groups. The exposed horns fill the gap with B♭–B♭–B♭–E♭–F–B♭ in bars 59–62, keeping the opening rhythm but widening its intervals. At 63, quiet violins begin B♭–E♭ over G and E♭ in the inner strings. The horns’ held B♭ carries across the change from call to dolce melody.
transitions.evidence: The E♭-major-group boundary is bar 59 at 51.987 s; the analysis marks a boundary at 0:50 and lower relative level thereafter. Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1: violinoone.ly, violinotwo.ly, viola.ly, violoncello.ly, oboi.ly and fagotti.ly establish bars 56–58 and 63; cornies.ly writes G–G–G–C–D–G for horns in E♭, sounding the stated call. score.json supplies bar assignments and the bar-56-to-67 span. The quiet violin entrance is a provisional alignment, not an ear-checked onset.

transitions.title: Two silent bars reset the opening
transitions.how: Three short B♭-dominant attacks in bar 121 resolve to E♭ major in 122: bass B♭–E♭, with D rising to E♭ in the first violins. Two complete silent bars follow. The repeat then replaces that full E♭–G–B♭ chord with the opening’s bare G–G–G–E♭, restoring the C-minor argument without a connecting modulation. The orchestral chord has become a unison gesture, and its fermata interrupts the pulse again. The silence is written into the exposition’s ending, not an extra pause invented for the repeat.
transitions.evidence: The Exposition repeat boundary is bar 1, occurrence 2, at 102.587 s. Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violinoone.ly, violinotwo.ly, viola.ly, violoncello.ly, oboi.ly, fagotti.ly and cornies.ly end the volta with the bar-121 dominant, bar-122 E♭ chord and R2*2. The opening strings restore the repeated Gs and E♭ fermata. The analysis’s 1:40 window has reduced relative level; the form relation independently matches the opening at a 102 s offset. Bar timing, rather than that fixed offset, anchors this provisional join.

transitions.title: The same silence opens another key
transitions.how: The E♭-major cadence and two silent bars recur, but the next call changes the destination. In bars 125–126 the horns take B♭–B♭–B♭ down to G; strings answer with D♭–D♭–D♭–C against that held G. D♭ and G briefly form a tritone before C arrives. After the fermata in bar 128, quiet second violins and bassoons establish F minor in bar 130: A♭ above F and the cellos’ C. The opening rhythm crosses the boundary, but the exposition’s C-minor-to-E♭-major route does not restart.
transitions.evidence: The Development boundary is bar 125 at 203.053 s, beside the analysis’s 3:24 novelty boundary. Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1: cornies.ly supplies sounding B♭ and G; violinoone.ly, violinotwo.ly and violoncello.ly supply D♭–C and the fermata; fagotti.ly, violinotwo.ly and violoncello.ly give F–A♭–C at bar 130. The preceding rest bars are 123–124, occurrence 2. score.json supplies the bar-120 occurrence-2 to bar-130 span. Timing remains provisional; audio key estimates are not the harmonic evidence.

transitions.title: Two-note replies shrink to isolated chords
transitions.how: In bars 196–203, winds and strings exchange pairs of minim chords instead of repeated quavers. The strings give C7 over G, then F minor over A♭ in bars 198–199. The exchanges contract further: B♭ minor, C♭ major and D♭ major each pass from winds to strings in bars 209–214, one chord per reply. Both groups settle on F♯ minor in 215–220. C♯ then rises to D while F♯ and A remain, producing D major in 221–227. This liquidation removes the motif’s rhythmic detail; the diminuendo reduces its weight without changing the metre.
transitions.evidence: This is an internal seam within the Development section, anchored at bar 196, 257.230 s. Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violinoone.ly, violinotwo.ly, viola.ly, violoncello.ly, oboi.ly and fagotti.ly write the alternating minim blocks, the stated chord tones and diminuendo/sempre più piano/pp markings. score.json assigns their bars and supplies the span through the start of 228. The analysis has boundaries at 4:16, 4:24 and 4:28, with lower relative level at 4:30–4:35. These support the thinning passage, not independently identified chords. Timing is provisional.

transitions.title: Diminished chords recover the opening rhythm
transitions.how: Winds and strings trade B–D–F–A♭ in bars 233–240: the diminished seventh on C minor’s leading note. In the string replies, cellos have B, violas F, and violins D and A♭. These quiet blocks break into fortissimo A♭–A♭–A♭–F fragments, progressively compressed into running quavers. At bar 248 the bass turns from F to three G attacks; bar 249 answers on E♭ under a fermata. The recapitulation arrives by recovering the motto’s rhythm from the fragmented texture, not through a long G-bass dominant pedal.
transitions.evidence: The Recapitulation first-group boundary is bar 248 at 295.749 s. Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1: oboi.ly and fagotti.ly exchange diminished-seventh notes with violinoone.ly, violinotwo.ly, viola.ly and violoncello.ly in 233–240; the same parts restore A♭–F fragments and F–G–G–G in 240–248, then E♭ in 249. The span runs from bar 232 to 253. The analysis’s strongest boundary is at 4:44, followed by high relative level at 4:50–4:55 and another boundary at 4:56. The score, not those broad windows, identifies the provisional return.

transitions.title: A half cadence becomes an oboe solo
transitions.how: The first group reaches a half cadence on G major, G–B–D, in bar 268. Instead of releasing the fermata straight into the next motif, the strings stop and the oboe keeps G alone. Its written Adagio descends F–E♭–D, curls through E♭–D–C–D, then repeats the descent to another fermata on D. With the bass absent, one line extends the dominant arrival without a new accompanying progression. The violins restart the familiar repeated A♭s falling to F in bars 269–270: the interruption changes texture and tempo, not the material used to resume.
transitions.evidence: This interruption lies inside the Recapitulation first-group section. score.json places bar 268 at 314.496 s and bar 269 at 324.768 s; the analysis identifies a 5:16 boundary and low relative level at 5:15–5:20. Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, oboi.ly explicitly writes the G fermata, Adagio and descending solo; the string parts stop after their G-major attack and violinoone.ly resumes A♭–F. The entire cadenza belongs to bar 268. Its short-note timings and fermata releases are provisional and have not been checked by ear.

transitions.title: Bassoons redirect the call towards C
transitions.how: The earlier E♭-major route is rewritten. After the silent bar 301, G–B–D over a B bass in 302 supplies C’s dominant. Bassoons, not horns, give G–G–G–C–D–G in bars 303–306. Their held G carries into bar 307, where quiet violins begin G–C–B–C above E and C in the inner strings. The call and lyrical melody are transposed down a minor third from the exposition. The seam keeps its pause, repeated-note rhythm and dolce arrival, but now the second group begins in C major rather than E♭ major.
transitions.evidence: The Recapitulation C-major-group boundary is bar 303 at 349.659 s. Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, fagotti.ly writes the call and held G; violinoone.ly, violinotwo.ly, viola.ly and violoncello.ly establish the rest, G/B chord and C-major violin entry at 307. Compare cornies.ly and the strings at 59–66. The analysis shows reduced relative level at 5:50–6:05 and estimates G then C as local centres; written notes establish the harmony. The quiet passage’s automatic timing remains provisional.

transitions.title: The cadence becomes the coda’s first chord
transitions.how: Bar 373’s G-major chord resolves to C major in 374, with bass G–C and the first violins’ B–C. But that cadential arrival also begins the coda: no closing rest separates them. High C alternates between held notes and tremolo while the cello bass changes every two bars, C–A♭–E–F. Inner strings make the harmonies C major, F minor over A♭, C major over E, then F minor. The same upper C belongs to each chord; changing the bass and alternating E♮ with A♭ prevents the tonic arrival from becoming a stopping point.
transitions.evidence: The Coda boundary is bar 374 at 402.176 s. Mutopia 941, Symphony5_1, violinoone.ly, violinotwo.ly, viola.ly and violoncello.ly write the G–C cadence and the four two-bar harmonies in 374–381; oboi.ly reinforces the high C. The span uses bar-370 and bar-382 times. The analysis’s 6:40 and 6:45 windows show increasing relative level and a shift towards F-minor pitch content, consistent with the written change. The form relation matches the preceding transposed closing group, not a literal repeat of this coda. Timing is provisional.

facts: Christian Gottlob Neefe in Bonn; Haydn, Johann Georg Albrechtsberger and Antonio Salieri in Vienna
Bonn until 1792 · Vienna and its surrounding villages thereafter
Nine symphonies · five numbered piano concertos · 32 numbered piano sonatas · 16 string quartets · one opera
Progressive hearing loss documented in letters from 1801; conversation books used from 1818
composer.background:
Beethoven was born in Bonn in 1770, probably on 16 December, and baptised on 17 December. His father Johann sang in the electoral court chapel, and his grandfather Ludwig had been its Kapellmeister. The family name came from the Low Countries; the ‘van’ did not indicate nobility. Johann attempted to present his son as a child prodigy, but Beethoven’s more substantial training came from Christian Gottlob Neefe, who introduced him to Bach’s keyboard music and helped him obtain work as an organist. Playing viola in the court orchestra also gave him practical knowledge of instrumental and operatic repertory.

The Bonn years supplied more than a musical apprenticeship. The court of Elector Maximilian Franz, educated patrons and friends such as the Breuning family brought Beethoven into contact with Enlightenment literature and social ideas. After his mother’s death in 1787 and his father’s worsening incapacity, he assumed increasing responsibility for the household. In 1792 he left for Vienna to study with Haydn. The intended period of further training became permanent residence: the French occupation of Bonn in 1794 ended the old electoral establishment to which he might have returned.
composer.epithet: A pianist who turned small rhythmic cells into long arguments, then rebuilt the forms that contained them.
